details: The package ships an 846-byte `index.js` that runs automatically at install time via `postinstall: node index.js`, and provides no other functionality despite its name mirroring the widely used `use-sync-external-store` package. The hook prints the host name and working directory to stdout, generates a random UUID, and sends an HTTP POST to hxxps://webhook[.]site/b4ea4473-01d9-4763-9e39-3b02063219d5 with the JSON body {"event":"authorized-poc-test","testId":"<random-uuid>","status":"executed"}, then logs the HTTP status. The callback body carries only a random identifier and a status string; the package does not read environment variables, credential files, npm configuration, wallet data, or file contents. The publisher-declared description is "security testiong only" and the log lines are prefixed "[POC]", consistent with an install-time beacon probe published under a combosquat name to confirm that install hooks execute in target pipelines before a payload is staged.
